name: Stamp impact for state changes

source.description: An inspected explainer marks failures and expiries with labels that slam down like rubber stamps.

technique: A short uppercase state label lands from large scale with a tilt and a tiny squash, sometimes jolting the card it hits. The physical metaphor (an official stamp) makes a state change feel final.
purpose: Announce a state change in a diagram or story (DOWN, EXPIRED, DONE, SOLD OUT).
visual_behaviour: Label appears oversized and drops to size in about 0.2 s, overshoots slightly, settles tilted; the hit card shakes.
mechanics: power4.in scale-down, 50 ms squash, back.out recovery, four-step x shake of the target.
failure_modes: Stamps over important text hide it

provenance.observed: DOWN and EXPIRED labels land on hatched cards as a machine fails and a lease runs out.

evidence.notes: DROPPED stamp lands and settles tilted over runner C.

licensing_notes: Technique only, learned from a user-supplied reference (inspiration-only, rights unknown). Labels and layout are original.
